utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Are there matters you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing in particular, Mr. May. I just wish to say that I sent the message yesterday that I would come today, though I have not fully recovered, because we had started with the witness, so I thought I should make the effort. Last night I was informed by my associate that he has been interrupted and that now we are going to hear someone else, who should have been fifth. So it only shows that no rules or fair play are being respected. I'm not making any requests in that connection, I just wish to make it known for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You should have been told sometime ago that Witness B-024 was excused with the permission of the Trial Chamber, having been here for several days and having urgent matters to attend to at home. Now, the reason that the order is changed is because of the interruptions occasioned by your illness. Now, we will hear B-1775, we will hear B-024 when he's back. Perhaps we can hear something about that from Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we -- B-024 began his travels home before we were notified that the accused would be attending court today, and we did make an attempt to secure his presence. His -- the visa that he was given to attend his original testimony was a single-entry visa so we had to reapply for a visa. Today is a national holiday in Holland, as I believe tomorrow is as well. I'm informed that it is not possible to apply for that visa until Monday. We expect him to be back in The Hague on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls B-1775. Your Honour, while we're waiting for the witness to come in, if I may make a suggestion that may save just a few minutes of time: The Prosecution intends to show this witness a video. The video depicts this witness himself. Given that he has protective measures by the Chamber, it would require the blinds being lowered in order for us to show the video in such a way that would not compromise his identity. What I am proposing is that I be allowed to complete my examination-in-chief, which I believe will only be 15 or 20 minutes, that we begin with the cross-examination, and then, just prior to the break, the morning break, if I could be allowed to reopen my examination for the limited purpose of showing the witness the video, in that way, at that point in time the blinds have to be lowered anyway. But I'll be guided by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I think we might as well have the evidence in one, in fact, rather than break it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can simply lower the blinds to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I solemnly declare that I will tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we begin, could I ask that a binder containing 12 exhibits I intend to use with this exhibit be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Prosecution Exhibit 452.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to begin your testimony today by taking a look at Prosecution Exhibit 452, tab 1. I'd ask you to look at the name printed on the first line of that document and simply ask you, is that your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You need to answer verbally so the record can record your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does that document also contain details about your educational and professional background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I would like to tender a Prosecution Exhibit. It's the 92 bis package for this witness. I would ask that it be assigned a number for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 453, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, the Chamber, as well as the other parties to this proceeding, have your statement before them and have -- had an opportunity to look at it before your testimony here today. I want to simply ask you some questions of detail regarding your statement. The first matter of detail I would like to ask you about is, I want to draw your attention to approximately the 5th or 6th of April. During that time -- or around those days, did you attempt to enter Zvornik from Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there ever come a time when you attempted to cross between Bosnia-Herzegovina and Serbia in which you were prevented from doing so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what, if any, border control or police presence there was on the bridge connecting Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: The police -- there was a police control. The police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the police, were the police Serbian police or Bosnian police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were directed by one of Arkan's men to collect corpses in the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the person who gave you that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Pejo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when was it that he told you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: On the 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to describe in general terms what this task involved. What did you have to do with respect to this direction by Pejo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: To collect the dead bodies in town and in the surrounding villages and to drive them to a particular spot, that is, to Alhos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness view a video. It is tab 3 of Prosecution Exhibit 452. It does involve a depiction of the witness, so I'd ask that the blinds be lowered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't believe it's technically necessary to go into private session. What he says is perfectly acceptable to be in open session. And if I could simply remind the director: This exhibit we will be tendering under seal and ask that it not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask that the video be played now. I'm going to ask you to look at the video, and then I will ask you to describe what is depicted after the video concludes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you play the video now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the collection of bodies in town. This, too, is collecting of bodies near the municipality building -- no. Actually, this is near the Njegos coffee bar, where we collected bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was that you that was visible in the video, collecting those two bodies that we saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I am there too. Yes, I am there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many bodies altogether did you collect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: During the first few days, about 10 to 15. And in -- over a period of a couple of days, we collected about 100 bodies and drove them to Alhos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no need for the blinds to be down. I don't know if it's the Court's wish to raise them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'm going to ask you just to clarify your last answer. You were asked about how many bodies you collected, and the answer as recorded was: "During the first few days, about 10 to 15." Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. In one day. That was in one day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So it should be "during the first day, about 10 to 15."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And then it goes on: "Over a period of a couple of days, we collected about 100 bodies and drove them to Alhos."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: When you say "a couple of days," can you give us a precise sort of answer, how many days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe five or six days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, out of the -- of the hundred bodies that you were involved -- approximate hundred bodies that you were involved in collecting, can I ask you to describe for us or estimate for us the -- approximately how many were men, how many were women, as well as approximating for us the different ages or age ranges of the people who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: They were all men, and they were between about 25 to 65 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And of these hundred or so men, approximately how many were in -- dressed in military uniforms or had any evidence of having been armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: About one half were in civilian clothes and the other half in military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you said that the bodies were brought to the Alhos factory. Once they were brought to that factory, did anybody conduct an examination of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: A doctor, a pathologist, Zoran Stankovic, came from Belgrade. He examined the bodies, and we would wash them for the postmortem, and if there was any information about them, he kept it so that it would be possible to find them if somebody came looking for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stankovic conduct a postmortem of all of the bodies that you collected, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Not all of them. He examined those bodies for a couple of days and not the others. This was just the environs of Zvornik. The bodies from Zvornik were buried at the Zvornik cemetery, so that if family members come looking, they would know where they are. They were buried according to the regulations, in sacks, and the tombs were marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During Dr. Stankovic's examination of the bodies, did he or assistants take notes about his observations of -- that he made during these postmortem examinations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, they did keep notes, and there are documents with those notes; how they were killed, whether the shots were from the front or from the back, whether they had any scars on them, on hands or legs that would distinguish them and that the family could recognise them by.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that Dr. Stankovic was from Belgrade. Was he associated with any organ of the government that you know of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I don't know. But probably he was. He couldn't have come on his own just like that. And No. 1 and No. 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your Honour, for -- the witness had expressed some concerns about talking about some people in that it would reveal his identity. If I could refer the Chamber to tab 2 of his binder, and could I ask that a copy of that be placed before the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you've just given us the numbers 1 and 2. Are you referring to the names -- or the people named on this list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if I could ask that that exhibit be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe for us these people, number 1 and number 2 on tab 2 of 452. Could you tell us, what was their involvement in the postmortem examination of these people, these bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: They didn't participate, but they were the most important people in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you -- again, the Chamber has your entire statement, but if I could ask you to simply list the different locations from which you yourself participated in the collection of bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Kazambasca, Glumina, Sahbegovici, Kamenica, Liplje, Divic, Drinjaca, Kozluk, Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to take a look at some photographs and ask you if you would describe for us if you recognise what is depicted in these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise to the Chamber; some of these will be out of order in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But if I could refer you first to tab 11 of Prosecution Exhibit 452, and it should be displayed on the screen in front of you. Do you recognise what's depicted on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: This is Alhos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that's the place where you brought the bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where precisely were the bodies kept at Alhos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Behind this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that you now take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 452, tab 5. Do you recognise what's depicted here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: It is the part of Alhos behind, from the back, from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does this picture show where the bodies were kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: You can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd now ask you to take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 452, tab 6, and tell us whether you recognise what's in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe the witness is having trouble with glare from the lights. If it's possible for the usher just to hold a folder.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: It's a bit too dark for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you have a spare copy that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll hand it out now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to show you the photograph itself. And can you tell us what's depicted there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. This is also Alhos, but from the other side, from the other side. It's also Alhos. Behind this building, that is where the bodies were placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, there are two buildings depicted in this exhibit, one with a flat roof and one with a peaked roof. Which building are you referring to as the location where bodies were kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: The one without the roof. That one, without the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask now that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 452, tab 9. We'll display it on the monitor but provide the original photograph to the witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: This is the technical school at Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to briefly describe how many times you were called to collect bodies at the Karakaj Technical School.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly, but roughly it was about 15 times. Perhaps less; perhaps more. Because there was a couple of other groups or teams for picking up the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And over what period of time did you go to Karakaj Technical School and collect bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer, but it was May or June, I think, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how many bodies in total did you collect from Karakaj Technical School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer, but it was approximately 100 to 150.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you please tell us in general terms, or estimate for us, the sex of the corpses and the ages of them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there men and women corpses that you collected? And can you also tell us the ages of the people that you -- of the bodies that you collected.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: They were only men. And their ages ranged from about 18 to about 70 or 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to see some of the injuries or injuries on some of the bodies? And if so, please describe.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I wasn't able to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you bring the bodies that you collected from Karakaj Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Technical School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: They were driven to Gero's slaughterhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe where Gero's slaughterhouse is with respect to downtown, or the centre of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Well, from Alhos, you go on for about 3 kilometres towards Loznica and Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Gero's slaughterhouse. When you say "slaughterhouse," are you referring to a meat processing plant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No. It was actually a slaughterhouse attached to -- well, when the war started, that's where they brought in the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to the war, this place was used to kill cattle and other animals used for meat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What would you do with the bodies once you brought them to Gero's slaughterhouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: They were driven off to Sahbegovici, where they were buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you look at another photograph. This is tab 12 of 452. I'll have the original handed up to you and a copy will be displayed on the monitors. And I'd ask you, sir, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: This is the school in Drinjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you have occasion to collect bodies from this school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many, and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Well, there were about 80 to 100 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And during what period of time did you collect these bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't give you an exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you this: During the time that you collected bodies from the school and from the Karakaj Technical School, was there active fighting going on in those areas between armed forces at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: There was fighting in Drinjaca. That's where the battles were taking place. Whereas here, in the technical school, there wasn't any. They were just brought in there and detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 10 of 452, another photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And sir, I'd ask you, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: That's the slaughterhouse that was known as Gero's slaughterhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'd ask you to take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 452, tab 7, and ask you, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: This is the Dom or centre in Celopek, where people from Divic were held in custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you collect bodies from this location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately how many and when, if you are able?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I can't tell you the time, but I myself carried about 20, transported about 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd now ask you to take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 452, tab 7 -- I'm sorry, tab 8, and ask you, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: That's the agricultural concern, the factory farm, Ekonomija. And there were bodies there too. And I drove them off from there -- I drove about 15 bodies away from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Well, it was somewhere around June, July, thereabouts. I'm not quite sure, because a lot of time has gone by since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us at the time that you collected bodies at the Ekonomija farm whether or not there were active conflict going on in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And to draw your attention to the time when you were collecting bodies from the Dom culture centre at Celopek, were there active hostilities in that area at the time you collected bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you look at another video clip. And at the end of -- at the conclusion of the video clip, I'll ask you a few questions about whether you recognise this location. If you'd look at the monitor before you and tell us if you have any difficulty seeing it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are Glumina. This is Glumina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 452, tab 4. Sir, while we are watching this video, can you tell us what you know about what occurred at the site of this video.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Well, that's where about 200 to 250 bodies were buried in sacks, and they were numbered and they were in two rows.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you involved in carrying bodies to this location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And as best you're able, can you tell us when it was that you carried bodies to this location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I think it was roughly in 1992, towards the end. 1992, the beginning of 1993 perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, before I ask you to conclude your testimony, I'm going to ask you to take a look at a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that it be placed on the ELMO. This is a photocopy of Prosecution Exhibit 336 that bears the markings of this witness. It is pages 28 and 29 from that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to take a look at the map on the platform before you. If you look to your left, sir, you can see the -- the actual map itself. Not the TV screen but the table to your left. Did you make the markings on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please point to the different markings you made on this map and just briefly tell us the significance of the different markings that you made.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Celopek, that is the cultural centre or Dom Kulture. Sahbegovici, that is the burial ground, the site where they were buried. And then Crni Vrh also; Glumina, Kamenica, Drinjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, there is a note at the bottom of this map. Is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what it is you wrote on the bottom of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: "On the copy I have marked in the types --" "On the copy, I have marked the places which I mentioned in my statement."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, may I just take a moment. And please bear in mind the fact that I -- in the list of witnesses that I have and that you have, that was provided me yesterday with the new order of witnesses, in fact, saw that it says here that the examination-in-chief of this particular witness would last up to three hours, that it comes partially under 92 bis but it includes this phrase "up to three hours," so that I have more questions to ask him than Mr. Groome raised during the examination-in-chief and the time he spent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we understand that. But let me point out one thing, that when you get these lists, and there is a time estimate - I think we've mentioned this before - the three hours, as I understand it, is a total time. It's an estimate made by the Prosecution. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. So it is an estimate that we would take one hour and a half of questions and allow an hour and a half for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 1775, you made a statement in 2002. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You'll have to speak up, Mr. Milosevic, with this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that. I can see I'll have to speak up. I'm doing my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You made your statement in 2002; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: About the events that took place in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you made your statement a full ten years after the events.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I said you gave your statement after a full ten years had gone by.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, can you remember with any precision everything that happened ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No, of course I can't. I said I couldn't be precise. Who could be precise and remember everything? Only somebody who makes notes and then can refer to them. But I didn't take any notes, so I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the last sentence be redacted, and if the accused wants to ask specific information about where he lives, that that be done in closed session -- or private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't understand why we should go into private session. He's not the only person that crossed into Serbia, I assume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Any detail which might identify, such as his address, we should have in private session. Yes. But unless you're going to ask about that, let's stay on in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're in open session, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I understood it that the authorities on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina detained you on your journey and crossing into Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They stopped you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it true and correct that at the time they said that you should stay on and defend the Serbian people? That's what you say on page 2 of your statement in paragraphs 2 and 4. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me this, then, now, please: Was the -- were the Serb people in jeopardy at the time and were they forced to defend themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So who threatened them? Who were they in jeopardy from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Well, the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that was in fact before the conflict in Zvornik took place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember that the day before that, on the 5th of April, in fact - because you're from the area and from those parts and I assume you'll know this - that in the village of Sapna, in the municipality of Zvornik, that an ambush was organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And Muslim extremists at the time killed Miko Stanovic and wounded a number of others in the ambush, other people passing by.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. There was this warrant officer that was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that the killing had been organised by the president of the Party of Democratic Action from the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on the Serb side, even at that time there was no reaction. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I assume that you will remember that the time you're testifying about is a time when there was great tension in those parts. Isn't that right, Mr. 1775?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the arrests that were made in mid-March 1992, the arrests without any reason of five Serb young men in Carmani [phoen] in Donji Kamenica, when Avdija Omerovic arrested them? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He mistreated them. And did that cause great unrest among the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Do you happen to remember - I assume you must know this - is it true that in those parts in that region, during the time that you're testifying about, that paramilitary formations were organised of the Patriotic League, the so-called Patriotic League of the Muslim extremists who called themselves the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it true and correct -- or rather, do you remember that in the area the organiser of this Patriotic League was somebody called Samir Misovic, who had a nickname, an alias of Captain Almir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And was his headquarters at Kula Grad, above Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was he linked and connected to Sahib Halilovic and Asim Hodzic, whose superior was a certain man called Karavelic? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So is that the structure of these paramilitary formations who had occupied Zvornik at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it also true that at the beginning the paramilitary formation in Zvornik was organised from the frameworks of the reserve formations of SUP, S-U-P, in order to cover up its true existence and the activities it was engaged in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please, do you happen to remember that already as of January 1992 - and I'd like to draw your attention to the fact that this was all as early on as January 1992 - that along the streets of Zvornik you could see and come across some criminals wearing police uniforms more and more frequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please, was it soon after that that it was made public that certain fighters for the religion were set up, led by the well-known Zvornik criminal called Mithad Grahic, and the unit was known as the Mosque Doves or Djamijski Golubovi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And did you hear that where they passed, they left dead people and burnt houses in their wake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you also remember that in the Zvornik area at that time another paramilitary group was set up which was called the Cobras, they were the so-called Cobras, commanded by a man named Suljo, who was a teacher before the war, in Sapna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about Sulejman Terzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then at the beginning of October, the commander appeared and his name was Semsudin and his nickname was Kobra, in fact. So most probably it was Semsudin Muminovic from Zvornik. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And he was later in command of the Zvornik Brigade in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the so-called army and brigade? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony and statement you explain that you buried or, rather, transported and buried parts of the corpses of dead Muslims; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That is to say, you did the -- you were engaged in the final act, the actual burial; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you that because I assume that at the end of everything that was going on, at the end of it all, then this -- the total number was roughly the number that you know about. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Well, yes, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell me this: Is it true that you took part in transporting the bodies of Serb fighters, those who had lost their lives up at the frontline during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as on page 6, paragraph 6 of your statement you say something about that. Is it true that during that period of time, the one you're testifying about, that you transported at least 5.000 - 5.000 - dead men's coffins of Serb fighters who had -- who were killed up at the frontline between Bijeljina and Vlasenica? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it also right that you conducted burial services for Muslims who died a natural death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in those cases they were buried with all the regular religious rites in regular, normal fashion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Is it true that the conflict in Zvornik began on the 8th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. But it actually began earlier on, but yes, the main thing was on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I've already asked you several questions about what happened before, what came to pass before, so I think that that's quite clear when you say that things began before that date. And was the immediate cause of the conflict this large-scale mobilisation on the part of the Muslim militia, police, which was ordered by the president of the municipality at the time and the member of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Democratic Action Party? He was a former dentist, Abdulah Pasic, and Nedzad Sabic was another one, the commander of the territorial staff of the TO, who was later commander of the 1st Podrinje Brigade of the so-called BH army. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that this mobilisation that took place was directed only against the Serbs in Zvornik and that the takeover of Zvornik was directed exclusively against the Serbs, because there were no other people there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Well, against the Serbs, particularly for Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said for the Serbs and particularly for what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: For Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. What you mean to say is to place the whole of Zvornik under their control and the environs as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise, in the autumn of 1991, these paramilitary formations, the ones which were organised by the Muslim extremists, armed themselves illegally. Do you know about that? Via the proprietor of this cafe which was called the Royal Cafe in Drinjaca. His name was Sead Hadziavdic, as well as in Kamenica through Saban Redzic and Esad Haskic. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that these Muslim paramilitary units, composed of these extremists of theirs, carried out mobilisation, captured Zvornik, after that the Serbs formed their own units in Celopek a couple of kilometres downstream from Zvornik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And at the same time, they evacuated women and children across the Drina to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So if my understanding is right of the sequence of events, Mr. 1775, the fact that the Serbs formed units and sent their wives and children to flee to Serbia was in response to the already carried out mobilisation and the capture of Zvornik by the forces of the extremists, the Muslim extremists. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that you arrived at Alhos. To avoid going into private session, you mentioned these two men that you said were the most important in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Though, Mr. May, I don't see that the mention of these two men would jeopardise the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you want to mention them, we will have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't mean his name, but names of these persons he says were leaders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, their names too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we won't mention names in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But please, Mr. 1775, those two, number 1 and number 2, who were the leaders, they were locals and officials in Zvornik for many years before that, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They were born there, educated there. That is where they lived, and they were there throughout; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 3, paragraph 1 of your statement, throughout that time, whenever you were free and you needed to do so, you travelled to Serbia normally, without any restrictions. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The first time you were assigned to go round town and, wherever you find a dead body, to collect it and transport it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In those days, was this after the conflict which had started on the 8th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: After the major conflict in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. That is when the attack took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: When you went around collecting them, you did not receive specific information as to where you should go but simply you went around town to see whether there were any bodies and where.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That was the conclusion I myself reached on the basis of your statement, so I just wanted to check it out. In your statement, on page 3, paragraph 5, you also say that in seven or eight days you had collected roughly 50 killed men of the Muslim ethnic community and the body of one Serb woman and one Muslim woman. And then today you repeated that half of them were in uniform and the other half in civilian clothing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So is this right; that in the first eight days, you collected about 50?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe more, but that is what I assume it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just checking, because I believe that what you wrote down and reviewed is surely more correct than what you say orally. Because a moment ago you said about 100. Of course, 50 could be included in the figure of up to 100, but isn't 50 more or less correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: That is the total number collected in Alhos, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You collected them, carried them to Alhos, and pathologists were there, invited by the Zvornik leadership, to establish how those people had been killed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since I assume that Zvornik, being a small town, doesn't have forensic medical experts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the leadership of Zvornik wanted the pathologist to establish exactly the cause of death of each individual who had been killed in the fighting in Zvornik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I am able to gather from page 3, paragraph 4 of your statement, you don't know anything as to the circumstances of -- under which those people were killed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were shot at too in Zvornik, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, while we were collecting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did they shoot at you from a distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: From Kula Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: While you were collecting the killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How far is that, Kula Grad, from Zvornik? I'm asking you for the sake of information that has nothing to do with your testimony, because it is mentioned in many testimonies, so I'd just like to know. I'm unable to find it on the map, this Kula Grad. It's probably not a toponym of any significance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: It is above Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the river or further back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: It is on the right bank, towards Sarajevo. From the Drina River, it stretches to the top, to the peak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it a village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a village, a Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We apologise. We didn't hear the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say on page 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can we remember to have a pause between question and answer. Otherwise, the interpreters are missing things. Just pause.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The bodies that you collected, according to what it says on page 3, paragraph 6 of your statement, were found at different locations, and there was one, two, three, four, or up to five bodies in some places; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. That is when we were collecting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then, as far as I'm able to gather, you put them in sacks and numbered them, and then those bodies were examined by the pathologists.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. First they were examined and then put in sacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The identified bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember that when the postmortems were carried out in those difficult conditions of wartime, a judge also attended and worked with the pathologists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that those pathologists established for each individual how those people were killed, whether they were killed in battle, from the front, from the back; they took notes and compiled reports. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You did not attend those postmortems nor the compilation of reports, I assume.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I was saying that you personally did not attend the postmortems and the writing of reports.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You assumed they did it, or did you see them doing it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that they were making reports and the pathologist was there, Dr. Stankovic, says, "I have the reports. Should anyone need them, let them contact me."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So everything was regular, under numbers, and in accordance with the rules, they were given proper burials.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge at all - any knowledge - as to the circumstances of any killing? You didn't witness any single killing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who killed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know in any single case what weapon was used to kill that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I assume it was a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's a logical assumption, but I'm asking you whether you know with any reliability what weapon was used.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it true that the Muslims that were examined by the pathologist and for whom a record was made, that you carried the bodies to the Muslim cemetery, which is called Kazambasca, as far as I see from my notes, in Zvornik? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this occurred in the course of April and May 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: This went on all the time. In 1992 and 1993 burials were taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the point is that the Muslims were buried at the Muslim cemetery, regularly and in accordance with - what shall I call it - the regular procedure applied in such cases.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the people who did it did this work in the same way they would have done it in peacetime; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, since you make some reference to this, on page 4, paragraph 1, when you were in Zvornik receiving food from the canteen at Alhos, that you shared that food with the Muslims who had stayed in their homes in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it also true that you were able and that even -- you were even told to do that, that is, to transport Muslims who wanted to go somewhere, that this was not prohibited, and that you were allowed to give them a lift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And those people - and I am referring primarily to Muslims that you transported and who left Zvornik - where did you drive them to mostly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: In the direction of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tuzla? To Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. Crni Vrh, and from there they went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please: They were leaving Zvornik of their own free will. No one was forcing them to leave Zvornik, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they left of their own free will. They asked you to drive them up there, as far as Crni Vrh. You do that, and then from there they go on to Tuzla. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say -- no, to avoid any confusion: We were talking about the citizens that you assisted in going where they wanted to go. Now, will you explain to me, please, since you took part in the transport, you participated in the final stage, that is, the burial stage; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And there were other people who would bring bodies to a certain spot, and then you would pick them up from there in order to bury them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this actually means --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: There were several groups collecting the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But at the end, they all somehow were dealt with by you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So during this main conflict in April, how many Muslims were killed in total then? Since you dealt with all of them in one way or another, how many of them were there in total during the conflict in April and May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Well, I assume approximately about 100 or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How is that when you collected only 50?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: They were collected occasionally. This lasted over a longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted you to tell me what happened in April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: I see, in April. In April/May, about 50, maybe a little more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Fifty or maybe more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. But this was a long time ago, and it's difficult to remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. 1775.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I wish to draw your attention to the fact that the previous witness, who was dealing with the media, had included in his so-called expert report that the Serbian press did not report on thousands of bodies in the streets of Zvornik, as reported by your employee Florence Hartmann. And I asked him, if you remember, how he could have put that in his report, that it was a fabrication. Here you are, you have a witness here who says that in April and May there were about 50 killed, and here you're using the figure of thousands of bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We are dealing with this witness and his evidence. Now, you've been told before you can make your points at the end, rather than just taking up time -- taking up time during the examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is fine, Mr. May. I just wanted to draw your attention that the opposite side knows the truth full well, and yet they're bringing witnesses who are putting forth gross lies. They have this witness for a year and a half, and they're fully aware of the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You also say -- but never mind. I won't ask you anything about that any more. I'm going to skip over some questions because, to tell you the truth, I don't want to go into all these details. I find the overall figures, total figure, quite sufficient. The fuel that was used and all the other requirements you had, was that supplied by the utilities company of the town, providing all these communal services for the town; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you worked with this utilities company and the communal services; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in the facility that was called Gero's slaughterhouse, for instance, was the procedure the same? I mean, with respect to the examinations performed by the pathologists, like it was in Alhos.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Only for a time it was. What was done and completed, we buried those bodies in Glumina. But afterwards, it wasn't done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume the procedure was the same when the pathologists Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But as the pathologists themselves weren't from Zvornik and weren't able to be there all the time, so this procedure was not undertaken when there were no pathologists there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about some other procedure? Was there any other procedure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you happen to know all the things that went on in those parts, the fighting that took place during those two months? But I don't want to ask you this in general terms. I don't want to tire you and make you remember all the details of what was going on. Let me just ask you this: Was it a general period when the Mosque Doves, the Dzamijski Golubovi, that we mentioned a moment ago, this group of people, when they would rove around town at night and the settlements round town and kill and loot Serbs and Serb houses? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember perhaps that this man Samir Misovic, who was known as Captain Almir - his alias was Captain Almir - that he was reinforced by an armed group from Kalesi [phoen] and Dzvinica [phoen], over 100 fighters, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember their leaders, Cazim Huremovic, Refik Ibrakic, Salih Malkic [phoen], Izet Smajlovic, Zijad Smajic [phoen], and so on, those men? Do you remember them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And for the most part, they would attack during the night -- not for the most part, but they attacked exclusively at night. They attacked the settlements around Zvornik, they looted the houses, burnt them down, destroyed them, and killed the Serb people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember an attack that took place on the 17th of April? If you don't remember the exact date, let me remind you of what happened on that day. These groups of Muslim extremists attacked a Serb village by the name of Rastosnica in the Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Killing Zoran Bogdanovic and a number of other people who were there. And then they looted the whole village and set fire to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that it was against the village of Boskovici, once again in the Zvornik municipality, that on the 5th of May an attack was launched once again by these Muslim extremists, and on the occasion they killed nine Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to read out their names here and now, but I assume you remember them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that on the occasion these Muslim forces were led by Semso Muminovic, Dzemail Spahic, and Hajrudin Mesic, nicknamed Labud or "Swan"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And straight afterwards, on that same day, the 9th of May, in the morning hours, before noon, they attacked the village of Gornja Baljkovica and killed another 16 Serbs and then fully looted the village and burnt it to the ground.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that the perpetrators are known? Do you know about that? Because at the time, people knew about this. Zvornik is not a big place. Ramiz Subacic from Memici was one perpetrator, then there was Jusuf Fargan from Kresivici, and the brothers Subasic Smajo and Smail, Dzigaric Husein, and Farid Kunzic from the Muslim village of Nezuk.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about whether any steps were taken to prosecute these killers? Were they held accountable anywhere and by anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you happen to remember another attack, one launched by these forces, this time in May 1992, on the Serb village of Rozanj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. It was Majevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were several attacks. And all the Serbs, the local inhabitants, had to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning they first killed this man called Dragan Asceric already on the 23rd of May. I'm sure you'll remember that. And then on -- during several attacks they killed many more farmers, and all of them had to leave the village, otherwise, they would have all been killed there had.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember the fact, for example, that once again, one and a half months later, in the next round of attacks on that same -- in that same region and that village, that Bogosav Ostojic, Mitar Ostojic, Stanko Ostojic, Goran, they were all killed while they were going to mow the meadows? Do you remember that taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So these were farmers, peasants, civilians going to mow the meadows and they were killed in violent fashion by the Muslim extremists in that village in July, when people and farmers generally mow meadows.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then Dusan Filipovic was killed, and Veljko Filipovic with him, and Ilija Lazic and Rajo Lazic, and the Muslim forces then proceeded to loot and completely burn to the ground the village of Rajo. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you also remember that on the 27th of May, when these same Muslim extremists -- not the same ones in person, but the Muslim forces that they had in Zvornik region generally, set up an ambush on the Sarajevo-Zvornik road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They shot at the Serbs working in the bauxite mines. That means they shot at ordinary workers who were on a truck.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on the occasion, Novak Sukic was killed, Zoran Popovic was killed, Djordjo Mijatovic, Stevo Simic. You remember all these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They were all workers, miners, from the bauxite mine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, in Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They were taken prisoner and later killed. These were Milomir Vujadinovic. He was killed. You remember that? And a worker, a civilian who was also held prisoner and killed only because he was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember on the 29th of May, when there was another ambush in the village of Sandici, on the Zvornik-Sarajevo road, when they killed Milosevic Milutin, and Jovo Blagojevic, as well as Dragica Matikosa, Miodrag Vorkapic, as well as Ivan Ivanovic, Dragan Petrovic, Vesna Krdzalic. Do you remember that taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. I did, because I had to go about the business of burying the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. 1775, I am asking you precisely the names of these people also because I know that you were the person who buried these individuals immediately after they were killed. So I assume that you had heard about them, because these were tragic events and it is impossible to forget them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you also remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's time now for an adjournment. Twenty minutes. Witness B-1775, could you remember during the adjournment not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over. And that does include the members of the Prosecution team. We'll adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'm asked to remind you, could you keep an eye on the microphone of the accused. And before you answer, could you make sure it's gone off. If you watch his microphone when he asks a question, see it go off, and then answer. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, you said towards the end of the last session that you would be giving me 20 more minutes. I understood from your first explanation that I would have at least one and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. It was the -- it was the adjournment which was 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. I wasn't listening, then. I wasn't listening carefully and understanding carefully what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. 1775, you've understood what's just been said? When my microphone is switched off, you start speaking. That's the technical side of it. But I'm sure you'll remember the village of Odzacina, the Zvornik municipality, when these Muslim paramilitary forces on the 20th of June launched a sudden attack on the village, killing Vaso Tanaskovic on the occasion, Kosta Kostic, Cvjetko Kostic, Smilja -- she was a woman, Smilja Tanaskovic. Jovika Tanaskovic, another woman; and several other unidentified individuals. Do you remember that event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember another attack on the village of Boskovici on the 1st of August, when -- the 1st of August, I'm talking about, I'm sure you'll recall the date -- when 26 Serbs were killed on that date alone in the village of Boskovici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you happen to know that these attacks were launched by and carried out by a brigade under the command of Semso Muminovic from the village of Vitinica, once he had destroyed the whole village? And this kind of destruction of a village has the character of genocide. So do you know that for this particular operation, the brigade was later given the name of knightly or Gallant Brigade, that they became known as the Knights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know about an event that took place on the 24th of August this time, when they attacked the Serb villages of Gornja Kamenica and burnt down all the houses there, even destroyed the cemetery, the Orthodox cemetery, killing Ljubomir Tomic, Dragomir Tomic, Milomir Kukolj, Radomir Kukolj? I assume you'll remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember also at the time, from Muslimansko Snogovo, the Muslim forces from Muslimansko Snogovo, Samar and Kamenica launched an attack on the civilian Serbian population in the Serb village of Snogovo, because there's a Serb Snogovo and a Muslim Snogovo. That's when these attacks were carried out. And on that occasion not only were civilians killed but there was heavy fighting in the area. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you'll remember the 24th of August, when the following were killed: Milovan Jasikovac -- he was killed with a baton. His feet were burnt. He was stabbed all over his body with a knife. His tongue was cut off, and he was also castrated. And they killed not only him but also Ilija Jasikovac and several other people. So do you remember these events taking place and what they did to those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember the fighting around Kamenica on the 28th of August, when the following were killed: Draga Kovacevic -- Drago Kovacevic, who was previously castrated. Rusica Josipovic; Milos Nikolic, who was burnt to death; Nedeljko Markovic; Zdravko Manojlovic, nicknamed Katovic [phoen]; Nada Mijatovic, Ratko Petrovic, Prelovac? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember this, the event that took place on the main road running between Zvornik and Sehovici at a place called Crni Vrh, when the Muslim paramilitary formations attacked a column of vehicles carrying Serb civilians? Twelve people were killed on that occasion, and I'm sure you'll remember that one of the passengers was a 21-year-old woman who was five months pregnant. She was hit in her stomach; the baby survived, but the mother died.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The other way around; the baby died.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember the attack on Novo Selo, when Milisav Ilic and Zoran Ilic were killed and Vestko Markovic [phoen], Lazar Ilic, Spasa Ilic, Ikonija Ilic, and most of them had their throats slit. They were killed not with firearms but knives. They were slaughtered and then their bodies burnt. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell me this, please, Mr. 1775: Do you remember the sudden attack against the village of Setici when in the yard of the Pantic house they killed Mihajlo Pantic, who was 90 years of age, and then -- actually, he was all cut up, an old man of 90. As the experts say, he was -- his throat was slit and his back was all cut up. Then there was Cvija Pantic; she was a woman and she was 82 years old. Savo Pantic, he was 72; Desa Pantic, another woman, she was 65 years old; and Ljubica, a woman, she was 46 years old; Bosa Lukic, another woman, she was 65 years old; and Cvija Prelovic, another one. Do you remember this slaughter, the slaughter of these old people and women in Setici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember the attack on the village of Malesici, when they killed Zdravko Malesic, who was 70; Mihajlo Peric, he was over 90 years of age; Cvija Peric, she was 90 years old; Ljubica Peric, she was 50; Draga Kulic; Sara Vidovic; Pero Milosevic; and another woman from Majevica who happened to be visiting in the village. All the houses in that hamlet, the Malesici hamlet were burnt, having been previously looted. Do you remember that, Mr. 1775?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, now, since you had occasion to be -- to see those bodies close up: Do you remember that during the conflict between the Muslim forces and the Army of Republika Srpska in the area of Kamenica, Muslims captured and killed a large number of Serb soldiers? And when the bodies were discovered, some of them had been beheaded; others didn't have their legs and arms, and some bodies were cut up in pieces. Do you remember all those details, how the Serb soldiers were mutilated and massacred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes. And there is footage of this at Vodjansko Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it true that some of them were nailed and had steel blades stuck into them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in this condition the bodies were found of Uros Kazanovic; Radoslav Grabovic, whose body had one leg and one arm missing; Vlado Grabovic, who had his head missing; Savo Djokic, who had also been beheaded and on one leg a chain was found around the leg; Radisav Macanovic, whose throat had been slit; and Radomir Pavlovic, whose head had been cut off; then Miladin Ascevic, and Dragomir Bozic, whose bodies had been cut up and heads cut off and broken, crushed with a blunt object. Do you remember all those events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes, I do. All this happened at Godzansko Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And one man's body was without eyes, ears, and nose; is that right? And on one a 6-millimetre diameter steel rod had been thrust through his chest and his neck, and legs tied with steel wire; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the body of Radan Pavlovic had been cut up in pieces, and Sava Kazanovic, who had been beheaded and his chest attached to a tree trunk with a nail. Was that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, let us look at some other things that you mentioned here. Is it true that there was, in Zvornik, a commission for cleaning up the battlegrounds? You speak about this on page 6, paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As I do not wish to mention any names, on page 6 in paragraph 10, you say that a certain man who was a member of that commission gave you instructions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1775
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
